events.title: agk port: a second game. Thunder Force IV matches the original on 7997 of 8000 frames on the host and reaches its first stage on the Amiga. What it needed: a stack from address 0 is the top of RAM; stop's interrupt mask is lowered and on the Amiga an interrupt the game didn't get puts it back to sleep; a call with its data after it keeps the old return address; rte is the 68000's (move (sp)+,sr; rts) and the Amiga's interrupt entry builds frames to match; tables of routines behind a base register and routine addresses stored as immediates are followed (14,000 to 42,000 instructions); old bytes that never ran are neither patched nor poisoned; $A10001 answers the region the header asks for. The checking build looks at the chips' events where the original's control flow was (Sonic 2 now matches on all 4000 frames) and has RECOMP_PORT_STOP and RECOMP_DUMP_AT; an unhandled exception on the Amiga is reported on the serial port

events.title: agk port: the game runs first and the picture is drawn in its waits. The loops where the game waits for an interrupt are found (a test of RAM and a branch back to it) and listed for the layer; the copper raises an interrupt every sixteen lines and, when it lands in one, the layer draws until the blank is near. The VDP's status reads in-blank while the game's vertical interrupt runs (Sonic 2's handler waited a frame for the flag when the Amiga delivered it late). DMA to video memory compared and copied in longs, scroll geometry only when its inputs change, tiles to planar through a table per palette line, whole sprite cells a tile row at a time. Stock A1200 with fast RAM, sound off: Emerald Hill's logic from about 30% of full speed to 70-90%. README: the Mega Drive port

events.title: agk port: the game's RAM and code can be moved, and the Amiga's loader moves them to fast RAM. The port is done a second time for a layout a megabyte on and every long that moved is listed (in the code and in the ROM image); the loader adds the difference and redoes the header checksum. Chip RAM is half speed under eight bitplanes: a stock A1200 with fast RAM went from a frozen screen to a running game. recomp/mdamiga: the layer works to a raster deadline with a minimum slice, carries an unfinished picture over the blank and shows it when whole (or after eight blanks), so the game's interrupt comes every frame; colours aren't regrouped while a fade moves

events.title: recomp/mdamiga: the sound is a mixer. Twelve voices (eight for music, two effects of two) mixed into Paula's four channels as two fourteen-bit sides, a sixtieth of a second at a time, on Paula's own end-of-buffer interrupt; samples stay in fast RAM, voices sound left, right or both as the Mega Drive had them. The stream carries up to twelve channels and where each note sounds. Emerald Hill had lost a harmony voice and the PSG parts to four channels

events.title: agk port: sound. The Mega Drive runner has a Z80 (recomp/md/z80.c) running the game's own sound driver, and game --sound-rip DIR plays every request the game can make through it and logs what the YM2612 and the PSG are told. agk/mdsound.py turns that log into Paula's terms: notes with their pitch and level frame by frame, each FM patch rendered per octave to a short looped 8-bit sample by an FM synthesiser in the build, drum samples cut out of the DAC writes, the four most important notes on the four channels, loops found from the notes repeating, and what each request is (music, effect, jingle, stop, fade) read from what it does to music playing. recomp/mdamiga/sound.c plays the stream on a CIA timer and answers the game's writes to its Z80. The ROM bytes only the driver read are blanked and used for samples; the sound goes on a second disk when it doesn't fit. Sonic 2: 28 pieces of music, about 250 effects

events.title: recomp/mdamiga: the hardware layer. Planes A and B as an AGA dual playfield of wrapping bitmaps the copper scrolls (pointers and fine scroll per line where the game's scroll table changes), cells drawn from a planar tile cache only when written or when their tile changes, sprites as masked tiles into plane A with the cells under them put back, fifteen colours per playfield grouped from the game's palette lines in use. The software layer stays as layer_soft.c. Sonic 2's SEGA screen and title come up right; the frame's work still runs over on a stock A1200 (it sits out the next frame when it does)

events.title: agk port: a Mega Drive game's code rewritten for the Amiga's memory map, checked frame for frame on the host. The analysis run (game --analysis DIR) records coverage, computed-jump targets, the ROM bytes read as data and every instruction that touches hardware; agk port rewrites the code (RAM moved, hardware operands through the layer's cell and calls, pc-relative data made absolute, word pointers brought over, old code turned into jumps to the new) and builds a checking runner (recomp/mdport) that reports anything still reaching for the Mega Drive's addresses; --learn turns that report into hints. Sonic 2: 47379 instructions, 3999 of 4000 frames identical to the original, no stray accesses. docs/genesis-port.md

events.title: recomp: a machine layer. The runtime splits into the shared 68000 + host (recomp/runtime: m68k.h, the interpreter, host.c with the window, PNGs, wav, record/replay, --coverage) and per-machine directories (recomp/amiga, recomp/md); the translation's two code regions come from the machine (bus.h REGION0/1). agk recomp --machine md --rom GAME.md builds a Mega Drive game from its reset vector: the first build interprets everything and gathers its own coverage (game --coverage), the next translates what was played. The Mega Drive chips: VDP (planes, window, sprites, DMA, H/V interrupts, HV counter, scanline rendering), pads, Z80 bus latches; no sound yet. Sonic 2 reaches its title screen.

events.title: Move the remake's challenges and chapter environment out of the goal window into band badges, follow walking units with the camera, fix the chapter 1 flank tip and animate flanking: the goal window now shows only the win and lose conditions; the challenges become three stars (empty = still open, filled = done, faded = missed) and the environment an icon with its name, in the bottom band left of the 대화 기록 slot in the framed screen (the title cartouche is only 266 wide at the narrowest view and the longest chapter title, 22장 · 신카루스 항구 안, takes 192, so badges there cut titles such as 16장 · 하스가나 사막) and next to the turn plate in the modern bar, where hiding buttons now reserves the title's real width instead of a fixed 120 and the environment badge drops to its icon when that hides fewer buttons; badge widths are measured, not guessed, and the badges get pointer-events back after all: unset (without it real clicks fell through to the map, which a scripted click did not show); clicking a badge opens its window (the challenges with turns left and the best record, or just the environment rule with a help link) and clicking again closes it, opening one closes the other, and the dim extra lines (both sides, see it in the confirm window, stars for what you achieve) are dropped as self-evident; a missed or completed challenge and the last turn of a turn limit show a short toast at the top of the map, and after the opening goal window a band across the map announces the environment once and the badge pulses; tune.json env gets an icon key; walking units push the camera when they come within 1.5 tiles of the map edge, in both editions; in chapter 1 the flank lesson no longer gets lost: surrounding a foe before the counter lesson opens flanking on the spot and its line and card follow that attack, and the turn-start flank introduction no longer counts toward the three tips per battle that used to drop it; on a flanked attack the allies next to the target (up to three) swing too, a beat apart, and 협공 appears on the target (green for us, red for foes); checked in the browser with real clicks in both screen styles, chapters 1, 11, 16 and 24, a 640-wide modern bar and the original edition's camera

events.title: Rewrite the in-battle tip cards and show affinity as icons instead of prose: each card is now one rule sentence, short points for conditions and numbers, and a dim last line only where the screen hint is hard to find, left-aligned, written apart from the help text and cut to what play needs (the user's wording review is applied, e.g. 반격 없음, 처치해야 함, 세 명까지 효과 적용, 방어 선택 시 해당 턴에 피로 회복량 감소, and the promotion card opens with 레벨이 오르면 경우에 따라 무기/방어구를 승급할 수 있습니다); key words are blue because bold does not show in the bitmap font; openWin can measure the real body height (fit) and any window taller than the map now scrolls its body with the buttons kept in view; the hover window drops the weakness/resistance line for trait icons (six races, flying, heavy armour, the six caster elements, new core/affIcons.ts), and the map 휴식 badge and the hover rest forecast go too; the help 약점·내성 table, the affinity card lines, the codex people list and both camp screens and the battle magic list use the same icons (bow, light, dark, wind, water, fire, earth, summon, song, prayer), weaknesses and resistances are green 약점 and red 내성 tags followed by icons, with a drawn green plus for an especially strong weakness, and the help topic gains an icon legend (races not yet met stay hidden) and the three opposite pairs; screen text says 턴 instead of 차례 (help, the mid-battle save notice, the 적 턴 빠르게 setting; character lines keep 차례); the 적도 같음 tag on help topics gives way to a sentence in each topic saying who it applies to (enemies flank only on hard, power and guard are ours only); events.title: capture writes into image.json the program that it ran, as the project path that it got, with the SHA-256 of that file, and release --file <image.json> records that PRG and its SHA-256 as the file and sha256 of the release with the bytes of the capture, so a README cites a file that git keeps and a reader can check, not the image.json in .c64-re-tools/local/

events.title: A JMP table of the idiom search ends before a JMP whose bytes a run wrote and whose opcode no run executed, so a stale copy of a jump table that the program later writes data over gives no table and no entry points, while code that a run wrote and then executed stays a table
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: compare --frames gives first: write for a range that a store writes first, also an indexed store such as STA (zp),Y whose dummy read the memory map marks: at a stop that shows a read and a write, the last instruction of the CPU history decides, a store with write and a read-modify-write with read, so a range that each release writes before it reads shows as run state; without that history the read stays first
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: The knowledge listing shows the memory that DXA, the decompiler and c64-source read, one definition in src/knowledge/program.ts: the segments and $0002-$03ff of the entry state, with the access, names, regions and comments there, and the hint of a range outside it names that memory, so code that a program executes in the zero page gets lines as the analyzers see it
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: ivm: for ...
events.author: yesco

events.title: An RTS table of the idiom search ends before the low or the high bytes of a table of an RTS dispatch start, and before an entry that a run wrote, so two dispatches on tables back to back each record their own table, and the screen codes after a table give no false references and no false code
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: release --base compares the knowledge with the segments of the file joined where they touch, by the same rule as the memory rows of the knowledge (mergeRanges), so a capture whose segments touch at $d000 or $e000 is the program of the knowledge; another byte or another range still refuses
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A $2c is a BIT skip only where the instruction in its operand bytes is 2 bytes long, because a BIT abs skips only 2 bytes: before a 3-byte instruction, as in LDA #$2c / STA abs after a branch to the STA, the idiom made the STA dual-use, and the listing then decoded its operand byte as an instruction
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: LAG_X, the MSX2's view lag in x for D3 (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D3, the user's choice, default 32): with the V9938 engine the view shown may lag LAG_X pixels (32-64) behind the camera in x before the cadence holds the ticks. msx/player.asm cam_lag: after cl_abs's test of LAG_MAX (32, as always), a lag of 32 or more in x holds the ticks only up to LAG_X when fb_eng is 1 (the V9938's two pages: an MSX2, or FORCE_V9938); the V9958's ring (fb_eng 0: the MSX2+ and the turbo R) returns as before, so their cadence decides as without the option. y keeps 32; rc_safe keeps RoboCop at least 16 pixels from the screen's sides (unchanged); D = 0 on the hold as the cadence needs (LAG_X - 32 below 256). From C/a_loop/lagx64.diff (x 64, y 32), which relaxed x on every machine: here the V9938 engine only. 12 bytes of the fixed area, none without the option. tools/mkrom.py: the option (32-64). tests/test_cadence_options.py: the option and its refusals, its code in player.asm only, its rule from the code (held from 64 px with the V9938 engine, from 32 with the V9958's, from 32 without the option). README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "Game logic". Checked: the 14 builds without the option byte-identical to a431d23's; the LAG_X=64 builds, 14, with the 12 known warnings; the code bytes read back from its product.

events.title: CAD_ADAPT, the cadence's option for D2's loop-3 (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D2, the user's choice, default 0): a picture that took fewer than CAD_ADAPT VBLANKs runs at most 2 game ticks, only a slower one up to CAD_MAX or CAD_HOLD. Loop-3 is CAD_MAX=3 CAD_HOLD=3 CAD_ADAPT=8 (3 ticks a picture only below 7.5 pictures a second at 60 Hz; the faster scenes as today); loop-1 is CAD_MAX=3 CAD_HOLD=3 alone, the options C/a_loop's analyst measured loop-1 with (its c3 builds and T_c3 trace builds: CAD_MAX 3, CAD_HOLD 3). msx/player.asm cadence: at cd_cap, with wf_n below CAD_ADAPT, a cap of 3 or more becomes 2 (C/a_loop/ad3.diff's rule; a cap of 0 or 2 stays): 14 bytes of the fixed area, none without the option. tools/mkrom.py: the option (0-255; refused with CAD_MAX and CAD_HOLD both 2, where it would do nothing). tests/test_cadence_options.py: the option and its refusals, its code in player.asm only, its rule from the code (2 ticks below 8 VBLANKs, 3 from 8 on; caps 0 and 2 untouched). README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "Game logic". Checked: the 14 builds without the option (product, drive, trace) byte-identical to a431d23's; the loop-3 and loop-1 builds, 14 each, build with the 12 known warnings; the code bytes read back from the loop-3 product.

events.title: FLASH_LOOK 7 counted in game ticks (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D1, still the user's choice, default 0): an enemy is white in the tick of a hit and the 3 ticks after it, and every hit starts the 4 ticks again, so hits at most 4 ticks apart keep it white. The first 7 counted pictures (white in the hit's picture and the next one); on the turbo R, at about 1.5 ticks a picture, Cain's hits came 3-4 pictures apart and the hold lapsed (58 look changes on the ground floor). msx/bob.asm: bob_begin, at every game tick's start (its one caller is player.asm gt_go), shifts each slot's fl_pend byte right; fl_note sets bits 0-3 (0Fh) and returns BM_FLASH, fl_held returns bit 0; no held-hit bit and no bob_skip test for 7: a hit in a skipped tick is still inside its 4 ticks at the tick shown for a frame of up to 4 ticks (tools/mkrom.py refuses FLASH_LOOK=7 with CAD_MAX or CAD_HOLD above 4). msx/rc2.asm's frame end builds no fl_pend loop for 7 (ml_tkd stays as the label). FLASH_LOOK 6 is unchanged (its own block, the same bytes). OS_FLASH, the results and everything the logic reads as always. Free bytes: the fixed area 22 more with 7 than without the option (product code_end 7E1Dh -> 7E07h; the first 7 cost 2), LC1 5 fewer (slot_clear, as before). tests/test_flash_look.py: 7's rule from the code (fl_note's store, fl_held's mask, bob_begin's shift; 4 white ticks for a hit, restarts, steady at hits 4 ticks apart, the pictures at 1-4 ticks a picture, a hit in a skipped tick never lost), bob_begin's one caller, no frame-end loop and no held hit for 7, mkrom's refusal; 6's rule as before. tools/mkrom.py's help, README.md's options row, docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "The hit flash's look" (the measured numbers of the first 7 marked as such). Checked: every build without the option byte-identical to a431d23's (the product, the 13 drive and trace builds of gate.sh builds); FLASH_LOOK 6's 14 builds byte-identical to a431d23's with FLASH_LOOK=6; 7's code bytes read back from the product ROM; tests/test_flash_look.py 7 passed, and fails with fl_note storing 07h or fl_held masking bit 1.

events.title: FLASH_LOOK (tools/mkrom.py): the hit flash's look, for the user's choice (docs/PERF2_PLAN.md D1; nothing decided, every build without it byte-identical: the 58 variant sets that build, the drive, trace and product builds). 6 = at most one white picture in 4 per enemy; 7 = an enemy stays white while hit less than 2 pictures apart and turns normal 2 pictures after its last hit. msx/bob.asm fl_note, fl_held and fl_due decide only the BOB record's look (bob_mode) per enemy slot and picture shown; OS_FLASH, the results and everything the logic reads as always. fl_pend's byte per slot keeps the held hit in bit 0 and the look's pictures to come in bits 1-4, shifted right at rc2.asm's frame end (ml_flc); a hit arms from bit 2 up, so every part of an enemy takes one look; objects.asm slot_clear clears the byte for a new enemy. No RAM of its own. Free bytes: the fixed area 164 -> 158 (6) or 162 (7) in the product, 100-119 -> 94-113 or 98-117 in the drive and trace builds; LC1 24 -> 19 (153 -> 148 in the level-1 trace build); the other banks unchanged. tests/test_flash_look.py (the option, where its code is, the rule from the code's constants); docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md "The hit flash's look" (what changes per level, the measured speeds and looks); README.md's options. Checked: the logic traces with FLASH_LOOK 6 and 7 (level 3's 16, level 2's 23, level 1's cov1, cov0, cov0_tr) 0 differ, lost counters 0; the look's rule without an exception on kill, boss and l2_barrel on the MSX2, MSX2+ and turbo R; make test the 4 known failures only.

events.title: Level 3's map-write caches (performance campaign 2, logic-1): a beam in its off phase (msx/level3.asm lt2_off) and a wall turret's panel and turret blocks (msx/level3obj.asm tur_put) no longer write the words their cells hold. Every map change counts in mw_gen (msx/tiles.asm atr_put's change path and fb_invf; msx/cold.asm tiles_init); each writer keeps an entry (per beam record bm_gen; per turret type and block the look, the cell and mw_gen) that stands only in the tick after its own use (mc_cur and mc_prev, aged by msx/special.asm hz_update at every tick's start, cleared by l3_init at every life) and only while mp_lost and atr_lost are 0, so a skipped write is one that would have changed nothing. tiles.asm cam_cells takes the cells with add hl,hl four times (the same B and C for every value). RAM 59 bytes (F170h-F190h, ECFBh-ED08h, EDF0h-EDFBh, msx/msx.inc); tools/mapcells.py checks the beam records against BM_N (7 of 7). docs/MSX_ARCHITECTURE.md (Map-write caches) and docs/LEVEL3.md 3.3. Checked: level 3's 16 traces against the bench 0 differ with the lost counters 0; make test with the 4 known failures only; 58 of the 61 option sets build (the three DEMO sets fail as before). Free bytes (product): fixed area 164 -> 168 (lowest set p_pzdiag 29 -> 33), LC3 4794 -> 4785, FRONT 1112 -> 1105, L3 3867 -> 3784, L3B 2383 -> 2238.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: MAIN message functions now use standard varargs while the full 518,656-byte executable and mandatory hash remain exact; two instruction-value checks cover 1,550 functions, with documented declaration and qualifier blockers still open.
change_details.after: Kilrathi Saga reconstruction now models Win32 shell byte views separately from the game modules’ integer flags and names more globals from DOS source while retaining an upstream-reported exact 518,656-byte executable match.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The preserved 1995 DOS source now ships playable Linux, Windows x64, macOS and web ports plus a compatible level editor; differential fuzzing also corrected the documented same-turn arrow/glass rule.
change_details.after: The preserved 1995 DOS source and modern ports now include mkpit, which compiles bounded text maps, legends and scripts into compatible PIT level files; playable-port status is unchanged.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active PS1 emulator/debugger now models CD-ROM pickup, spin-up, Init, Pause and GetID timing from SCPH-7001/9002 measurements and applies NTSC 480i DFE row suppression in both software and OpenGL GPU paths; independently unbuilt and unrun.
change_details.after: PCSX-Redux now clears GPUSTAT bit 26 throughout incomplete multi-word GP0 commands and GP0(C0h) readout until the final word, matching an added silicon-focused regression test; independently unbuilt and unrun.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Moria8 adds disk save/load playtests, retry paths and deterministic failed-run capture across its 6502/65C02 ports; released/platform status is unchanged and tracker-side execution was not performed.
change_details.after: Moria8 now treats truncated Commodore drive-status reads as lost, retries only probes that can issue a fresh OPEN, and fails ambiguous save status rather than reporting success; upstream playtest-disk scenarios pass across C64, Plus/4 and C128.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The reconstruction now records three passing Xtensa firmware profiles with exact size budgets and an original-ROM oracle with 14/14 scalar STRING cases observed twice; device execution and broad BASIC compatibility remain explicitly unverified.
change_details.after: The reconstruction now has a host-verified bounded C99 ESC/ANSI transport contract with malformed-CSI quarantine; original CPC ESC behavior, BREAK on device and a native hardware run remain explicitly unverified.

before: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification
after: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: MDFourier now uses amplitude-spectrum scaling in sample units, reports amplitudes relative to the strongest tone, and derives the digital noise floor consistently in dBr; the tracker did not independently build or compare captures.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Amy Studio adds ten explicitly labelled faithful COMPUTE! adaptations as ColecoVision examples, preserving source-game rules and quirks while remaining an original browser development environment.
change_details.after: Amy Studio adds Shaker and Star Strike as explicitly non-port ColecoVision adaptations built from 1986 Ahoy! article rules, plus compiler support for inline VoxPCM and variable shifts; they remain original adaptations inside the browser development environment.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port; its new editor pipeline has transactional room-source history, validated portal topology and collision/corner-wall rebuilding from original LEVELSAVE contracts, but complete-file assembly and playable newly drawn rooms remain pending.
change_details.after: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port; its editor now assembles complete original-map room graphics streams and preserves packed point-lighting animation controls, while new-geometry authoring and playable newly drawn rooms remain unproven.

events.title: scroll9958.asm: the ring's queued columns and rows draw only the cells still in the kept area (draw_kept, as swr_one's changed cells). A row waits while columns are queued (column first) and a column while a row is; the camera may move on meanwhile, and a cell it left shares its ring slot with one on the screen 32 columns or 16 rows away. Found with the static vats on the FS-A1FX (tour from 2385, the product's caps): a row queued at column 64 drew columns 80-81 over 48-49 when the camera had run to column 47, 45 pictures with two stale cells; with draw_kept 0 in 400 pictures on the three machines. tests: RingQueueTests

events.title: docs/LEVEL3.md: level 3's plan. The original (REA on build/ram/level3_full.bin and the bench): the way in, the header $86B4 and level_init's level-3 part (no gun opening, state 6, the fade's state 0Bh), the map (50 rows, floors, 106 tiles in view), palette C identical to level 2's (mean dE76 2.18 against 2.68), the beams (level_tick_2: two cells, 32/32 frames, 0Ch), the three two-part lifts, the turrets' map writes, act_20, the 39 spawn entries and the markers (type 0 spawns nothing, type 43's markers_off), the 20 types with their handlers, sizes (4,222 B of level-3-only code), deaths and frames, Cain as RoboCop 2 (invulnerable above y 290h, the launch mailbox, his death and the level's end), the bullets and debris, the 202 frames drawn (58 of 48 px or more), the sound (nothing new), the end and the hand-over (level_load_3 $86DE), nine quirks. The design: the descriptor's third entry, the flow's hooks, two logic banks (BANK_L3, BANK_L3B behind a trampoline), the 2 MiB image's rules, the free bytes now, a dynamic frame cache in page 2 for Cain and type 21 with a white hit flash, a per-level FIELD_ID0, the pool in place, ENEMY_CAP's types, RAM homes, the VRAM map, the tools and the bench. The checks, five steps (A data, flow and bench; B logic and C play field side by side; D Cain, the end and the sound; E acceptance) and 15 defaults, the risks. docs/level3/HANDOFF.md: the log of the rest of the game, step 2's section. docs/AMIGA_ANALYSIS.md: level 3's ledger. docs/ROM_BUDGET.md 7: the level-3 image and coverage done

events.title: Level 2's step 21, the code: CHEAT and the sound checks' tools. tools/mkrom.py CHEAT=1 (not with DIAG): cold.asm ng_init sets AG $804F FFh at each new game (the title's cheat handler $11F60: st.b $804F, REA), frame.asm fe_keys at frame_end's head maps F5 to key code 59h and F4 to 58h in $8032 while held, the code + 80h once let go (frame_end already acts on them: the original's F10/F9); there, in BANK_LC3, not in player.asm key_scan, so that the fixed area pays nothing (every set's code_end as before; LC3 -33 B, FRONT -5 B in CHEAT builds). sound.asm: label sf_back (no byte). New tools/bstest/fxlog.tcl: every PSG write (R0-R13), SCC write (9800h-98FFh, where it went) and OPLL write with the engine's events (requests queued, taken, ticks, stops, text screens, the stages' tune ticks), jobs fxl_jobs (level 2's drives tour, vat, mine, end, t1left, trolley on the cartridge's SCC, an SCC in slot B and the PSG alone; the continue; the briefings; both stages' visits); hz.sh fxbuilds. New tools/bstest/fxcheck.py: a model of sndplay.asm and music.asm's in-game effects replays every event from the logged state and compares each segment's writes, the queue's order, the tick divider, the end state, per effect its starts, refusals and plays to the end, the bench's requests per frame, the text screens' silence; visits (the stages' tunes tick for tick), selftest (mutations). New tools/bstest/cheat.tcl: a CHEAT=1 build by the keyboard from the power-on through both levels. variants.sh: the 5 CHEAT sets (53). Tests: tests/test_fxcheck.py (15), test_level2_rom.py CheatTests, test_bstest.py's count.

The plan's mechanism, rd_at's base in pz_tvb, was built first and rejected: its 113 T more at visit 1's entry moved visit 1's pictures (18 of 53 snapshots and 4 of 10 records differed from HEAD's); pz_tvb stays unused, C6AAh lv_voffy's. Harness: tools/bstest/stepcheck.py --visit 2 (visit 2's render; a snapshot's $8050 >= 2), check_all.sh passes it for solve2 and fuzz2; docs/HARNESS.md. Tests: test_msxpuzl.py test_visit_2 and the command line with --visits 1,2, test_bstest.py test_stepcheck_visit_2. Results against HEAD 7c8635a's builds: in 20 option sets only BANK_PUZL and the new blob differ (romdiff --blocks PASS); regress.sh check against HEAD's records PASS (45 verdicts, 0 FAIL); Brainstorm's 20 traces 0 differ (solve2 728, fuzz2 606 frames); visit 1 byte-identical (53 snapshots in VRAM, registers, palette and RAM, 10 records in every part); visit 2's 66 stills on the MSX2, MSX2+, turbo R and at 50 Hz equal msxpuzl.py render --visit 2, its records clean, board 0 in visit 2's palette and boards 1-3 in visit 1's (quirk 5); visit 2's flow from power-on into the range and the title PASS on the Expert and the turbo R; BANK_PUZL 4,483 B free (4,590), every other bank as before; option sets 46 of 48 (DEMO_ACTORS 2/5 as before); make test: the 4 known failures only

change_details.after: Spice86 now distinguishes redirected returns by stack level and carries SSA/data-flow through one IR pipeline, improving generated-method ownership without claiming perfect structure recovery.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active
change_details.after: Regenerator 2000 now indexes shared lexical-scope boundaries and performs monotonic block-range rendering while documenting the state and rendering invariants; upstream buildability remains established by the repository, not re-tested here.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Native Apple II collection; POM2 facade tests now exercise Apple //c and AppleMouse II firmware paths plus register, go and call control across game probes.
change_details.after: POM2 Games' native Apple II collection now records WARGALAGA II's 1.9 KiB memory recovery and Robot Space Station's tested DHGR-page code overlays; both remain named subjects within the collection.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Released Apple II and Commodore ports plus buildable/testable Commander X16 target; current main adds AI playtesting infrastructure with seven isolated platform stages and a broad set of gameplay-parity fixes, without tracker-side execution.
change_details.after: Moria8 adds disk save/load playtests, retry paths and deterministic failed-run capture across its 6502/65C02 ports; released/platform status is unchanged and tracker-side execution was not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; loop-wide sparse cells and canonical Dn pointer producers now survive only under proved write envelopes, while an A6 reader remains blocked at a cross-platform call predicate.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while connected homing, HUD, collision-retirement and world-record recycling continuations gain original-CPU fixtures; global alias safety and complete gameplay remain unproved.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v6.4.2 published; current devtools commit memory, graphics and assembler writes as one lease-bound machine change
change_details.after: konCePCja's KCPC debugger now publishes every frame through a documented shared-memory ring with sequence-numbered events and an independent fb_dump reader tested across Linux, macOS and Windows CI.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Firestaff's authenticated current-main startup matrix now passes four bounded real-media tests across all five games; Atari CSB rebirth/explosion rendering and executed-code CD-write tracing advanced, while Nexus playability and native display/input completeness remain open.
change_details.after: Firestaff now binds authenticated Atari ST Chaos Strikes Back archive members to the same original image and covers Atari ST 1.1 menu startup; broader native playability and Nexus completion remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: ASE now emulates the Mega ST RP5C15 and IKBD clocks with emulated-time advancement and snapshot state; Linux remains described upstream as untested.

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: Walls seen through other walls mid-turn fixed, the last two 3D areas remastered, and the comparison sheets revived. The blobber gave the painter's bias (0.49 cells nearer than the face's centre) to the faces facing the camera only, so while turning a face behind a nearer one at another angle sorted in front of it (New Phlan 3,11 turning W to N: a front face of the next cell over the temple's wall); every wall takes the same bias now (biasWall 0.48, a hair under its cell's billboards), so the walls keep their centres' order at any angle. Mountains (GEO 6/25) and the wilderness by the city (GEO 7/26) have remastered maps (phlan-poc/MAPS.md: every 3D area has one; make_textures.py's shape flag clears a texture above the original's per-column top line). compare.py renders the original's views with the test-only copy of its renderer (engine/classic3d_test.go, POR_CLASSIC) and the remaster's with the game itself from any square (POR_OPEN=map:NAME:X:Y:D, present/remaster drawOpen); the checklist's cause of the classic page corrected to the pane consts

events.title: Creation sheet: PNGs dropped on it, Add and Forget as cards, Modify on the sheet. The icon's poses stand on a dark grey ground and take a dropped PNG as the icon editor does (View.IconBox; takeIconPNG shared; the drop handlers belong to the page, newPage ends them; the editor sets its with each show), the portrait takes one as the sheet in play (ActPortrait while creating); the sheet draws itself anew (e.Act actRedraw). gpu.Drop carries the drop's screen pixel so the presenter picks the target by cell. The Add and Forget lists are cards of the portrait's head (a dropped PNG fitted) with the name and class beside it, laid out and paged by pickGrid (pickSaved, loadSaved; the bar's first word a parameter). Modify Character is the creation sheet on the member (editSheet, the loop shared with CreateCharacter; fresh keeps the items), Keep keeps the changes, Esc asks and puts the record back; the original's Raise/Lower bar and modifyDraw are gone. TestCreateSheet covers the drops, Add and Modify

events.title: Every screen fills the window (a hard rule, CLAUDE.md). The engine's page is variable (layout.go: textCols/textRows, winRight/winBottom/promptRow from them, 40x25 the minimum; setPageSize, Engine.cells); the presenter sends ActResize for the cells the window holds at the whole scale and stretches the page by less than a cell to the edges (grid, fit; a frame before the resize is letterboxed at the whole scale). resizePage keeps the page, redraws hooked screens (redrawWith: credits, sheet, journal, help) and relists the ones whose bar depends on the size (relist → actRedraw: pickers, designer, creation sheet, slots); the full-page boxes grow; TITLE pictures centre (fullPicture). pickGrid lays a centred grid of as many pictures as the page holds and pages the rest ("< page 1/2 >", clickable arrows, Next/Prev, PgUp/PgDn, wheel); the frame and the pointer only take drawn pictures. Windowed mode locked to 16:10 (gpu.SetWindowAspect; POR_WINDOW=WxH lifts it for captures); fullscreen keeps the screen's shape with the backdrop fitted. Credits in the engine (RemasterCredit); present/remaster credits.go and the fixed-page cell test gone

events.title: The analysis asks to correct the knowledge only for a refused seed in the program or an --entry outside it, as a routine outside the program can be code that the program copies there; a coverage gap is in-data only in a data range that the analyzer used; a second RTS dispatch through a recorded table gets its jump references, and a JMP run that overlaps an idiom is left out once
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: --fields finds a path through an empty list and names a cut list only when the fields show it; the listing and the source write a table entry with one function, so an RTS entry without a name is the address before its target in both; knowledge at reads the coverage of each map from one mask filled once, not from its range text at each address
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: assembler build --switch of main.asm writes the program also when the packed loader cannot be made, for a start screen of a captured stage, a segment below $0400 or a patch between the free ranges, and gives loader.written false with the reason; a missing Exomizer still refuses by name, and the loaded ranges and the start screen come from the same space as the switch defaults
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: Only a jump or call reference of the user or the LLM resolves a computed flow, and separate() and the export get the rule from one function: a JMP (N) reads its high byte in the same page, a vector is set by the code's own immediates only when no other write of the code changes it, and their values become reachable targets; an RTS or RTI after pushes is a flow too, with the target of two pushed immediates, else resolved by a jump reference of the idiom pass or the LLM; only a flow in code that a root reaches or that a run executed makes other code unknown; provenance separate lists each code region with reachable, executed and unknown, and the unresolved flows, so its --out file again holds every region, and a cut list of separate or leftovers names the --out file

events.title: renderer: 60+ fps fullscreen on the Win7 test machine, the picture unchanged pixel for pixel. The game draws straight into the window's frame (no copy of the screen a frame); wall faces are culled on the CPU by facing and frustum, in build order (sorting changes the soft edges' blends); a Fill of a whole image becomes the pass's clear; the sky and ground planes only test depth (beyond every face's depth, so writing it hid nothing, and the GPU now tests before it shades); gogpu's fullscreen flag is honoured on Windows; party cards cached per card. Battle view: -battle (POR_DEV=autocombat) has the computer fight both sides against eight monsters for measuring, the status line is drawn only when its text changes. Captures: the key script is paced by frames (deterministic frame for frame; ticks and frames interleaved differently each run), remaster ticks the view itself under a script, POR_FREEZE holds the frame for an outside grab, POR_OFFSCREEN forces the copy path, POR_SKIP leaves parts of the frame out (or undoes a saving) for timing and comparison; POR_QUIT runs play their keys too

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The Apple IIe/SoftCard environment now exposes kernel-managed W5100 socket and packetless TX/RX APIs, migrates Telnet to the kernel interface and adds a first working WGET client; network execution was not independently repeated.
change_details.after: Zapple-II / BP/M now includes a kernel-backed NETCCP remote-login server with Telnet option negotiation and terminal-independent command output; network execution remains upstream-reported.

before: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration
after: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: BO5 is reported 100% for its bounded boss-overlay scope, while the in-tree PC runtime adds most stage overlays and fixes menu/prologue text; upstream explicitly says PC coverage is incomplete.
change_details.after: Castlevania Symphony of the Night decompilation has begun RBO6 boss-overlay asset/entity recovery and corrected Saturn stage-15 sprite/table typing; broader PC and overlay coverage remains incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Version 0.7.1 adds whole-game m68k-to-C translation roots and overlays, exact display-gap comparison, a web engine and an interrupt-aware Paula state model; upstream reports 2,376 tests, but the tracker did not run them.
change_details.after: amiga-re-kit 0.8.4 fixes long-run CIA timing, A500-style 24-bit/chip-RAM address decoding and CPU-versus-Copper register precedence from Alien Breed II full-game runs.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v0.10.4 published; packaged demos now open from writable per-user copies, while Windows emulator integration remains explicitly experimental
change_details.after: PiST now analyzes TOS executables with persistent names/comments/code-data marks, live stopped-PC and Hatari coverage notes, picture inspection and source export admitted as a reconstruction only after vasm byte matching.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: ND500X documents and indexes the ND-5000 '87 extension: 23 of 25 manual-labelled instructions are represented, with explicit implementation plans and unresolved RHOLE/AMODB scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; six connected disk/media helpers and two shared service-state fields now have bounded roles, while physical-media behavior and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Wizardry VII reconstruction now routes maze sounds through a recovered semantic C routine; the pinned README reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%), with full C conversion still open.
change_details.after: Wizardry VII reconstruction adds named maze/region routines and derives typed data-file layouts from C declarations and recovered records; the pinned README still reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%).

before: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison
after: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Authenticated Nexus evidence now carries a retained retail BKR through Continue into a four-champion dungeon view, while FM Towns DM2 traces cover startup source frames; Firestaff-side Continue loading, HUD/viewport and presentation parity remain unimplemented or unverified.
change_details.after: Firestaff now hash-locks four authentic DM1 SNES cartridge images, decodes both H03 ROMDUNGEON slots and validates their shared 14-map structure; native SNES runtime, rendering, input and audio remain out of scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source and build workflow reviewed; independent execution unverified
change_details.after: DCTelnet now builds with m68k-amigaos GCC 16.2, and its GCC binary restores cursor-key navigation in the shell and Mystic BBS by correcting signed CSI-byte handling.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active Rust/C++ Amiga disk toolkit; decoded views now cover Workbench icons and indexed, EHB, HAM and 24-bit ILBM images with upstream corpus accounting and fuzz-bounded allocation checks.
change_details.after: Amiga Disk Engine now follows executable control flow into functions, cross-references and call graphs, names proven library calls, and exports source that GNU as rebuilds byte-for-byte across 39,363 corpus programs.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; the scramble/cutscene change now matches the original register allocation byte for byte, while the remaining strict-byte runs and whole-project completion stay open.
change_details.after: MAIN message functions now use standard varargs while the full 518,656-byte executable and mandatory hash remain exact; two instruction-value checks cover 1,550 functions, with documented declaration and qualifier blockers still open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Scoped PC-98 reconstruction now accepts 33 OP extents / 32 procedures / 4,370 owned bytes, including 487 initialized DATA bytes with actual-consumer and mutation contracts; whole-product source/link ownership remains open.
change_details.after: MAINL gains source-present DOS exception throw and global-unwind recovery covering 2,524 original bank bytes, but adds zero exact bytes; candidate size, EFLAGS and whole-TU gaps remain explicit.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: 1995 DOS source with modern compatibility layer and Zig build recipes. README distinguishes compilation success from incomplete SDL/audio and potentially crashing stub runtime.
change_details.after: The preserved 1995 DOS source now ships playable Linux, Windows x64, macOS and web ports plus a compatible level editor; differential fuzzing also corrected the documented same-turn arrow/glass rule.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Original Oric Atmos homebrew now shares one IVM bytecode generator and printer between its TPI compiler and parser, with constant-pool, accumulator and bounds checks consolidated in the same implementation.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Original Z80 development tooling now includes a headless CyborgOS platform alias and pause/state services; upstream compared 954 generated programs and platform outputs without changes outside the new platform scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: ND100X adds a disk-image CPU-identity editor that resolves SINTRAN symbols and segment pages from the mounted pack, ejects before patching, verifies the stored image and remounts it; upstream reports 37 focused checks.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact while six projectile-creator call contracts and their storage roles are restored; 24 orphan layout coordinates were removed, but broader semantics and minimum runtime requirements remain incomplete.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified

last_commit.message: NFS_DOS.EXE of EA's 1997 CD accepted too (a player's: "not the version ReNFS knows"). Its build, dated 17 June 1996, the same 1,254,591 bytes, differs from the 19 June one laid out and relocated only in the give-up branch of keys_control_word 0x48bec (the word written 0x000087a0, not 0xffff87a0; the function 4 bytes longer) and one German text at 0xe3814, neither read by the port: exe.c takes either FNV-1a (0x76078ed2, 0x21ef7c33). With every read checked against those bytes, the 1997 CD drew the same pictures in the front end, the four replays (equal at every snapshot) and nine races. Our CD copy has three bits flipped where the 1997 CD's bytes match their neighbours (NOTES §1). The message no longer says 1996.

before.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
before.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

before.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
before.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

after.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

before.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one. Fast RAM recommended but not required for release; debug executable requires fast RAM. Three original game disks required.

after.name: A1200 release
after.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one: 68020, AGA, Kickstart 3.x and 2 MiB chip RAM. Fast RAM is recommended but not required for release; debug requires fast RAM. Three original game disks are required. Network play additionally needs bsdsocket.library from WinUAE or an Amiga TCP/IP stack.

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: MEGA65 R6 (upstream-tested beta)
before.notes: README explicitly reports 0.4.7 beta tested on a real R6. Requires the board’s SDRAM, SD card, tos.img and user media. R4/R5 projects are advertised but explicitly untested; R3/R3A are unsupported. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is used as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

change_details.before: 0.4.7 beta; author-tested on MEGA65 R6, further hardware modes untested
change_details.after: v1.0 stable; upstream-tested on MEGA65 R6 and R3A; R4/R5 untested
